turns.content: For two blackbody stars, write L1/L2 in terms of their radii and temperatures. Simplify the radius factor when R1=1.5 R2.

The two objects have the same observed peak wavelength. Object 1 has negligible line-of-sight velocity, while Object 2 is receding at 700 km/s. Relate Object 2's emitted feature to the shared observed feature.
Use the physical relation connecting the feature identified above to temperature to express T1/T2, then substitute it into the luminosity ratio.
Check how the result would move if the quoted positive radial velocity were mistakenly interpreted as approach rather than recession.
Retrace the relation between observed and rest-frame peak wavelengths to verify the sign of the velocity correction.
State the resulting dimensionless luminosity ratio.
Describe the blackbody, feature-identification, velocity, and transformation approximations that limit its precision.
Compare the luminosity ratio with the radius-only factor and check the direction implied by a positive recession velocity.
Give the final ratio with a concise summary of the radius, observed-feature, velocity, and transformation models used above.
